title: Article 143 — Power of President to consult Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 143 provides that if at any time it appears to the President that a question of law or fact has arisen, or is likely to arise, which is of such a nature and of such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the opinion of the Supreme Court upon it, the President may refer the question to that Court for consideration and the Court may, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report to the President its opinion thereon. A special provision applies to disputes arising out of pre-Constitution treaties and agreements: the Court shall, as nearly as may be, report as in the case of a reference under this article (with historical nuances regarding justiciability).
content.glance: President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance to SC for advisory opinion. SC may report after hearing. Special rule for certain treaty disputes.
content.study:
Article 143 advisory jurisdiction:
(1) President may refer a question of law or fact of public importance to the SC; the Court may hear and report its opinion.
(2) Special provision for disputes arising out of pre-Constitution treaties, agreements, covenants, etc.

The opinion is advisory; it is not a binding adjudication between parties in the same way as a contested cause, though it carries great weight.

Examination: Presidential reference; public importance; advisory character; Court ‘may’ report (discretion in clause (1)); treaty clause (2).

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the SC.
2. SC may, after hearing, report its opinion to the President.
3. Special provision for certain pre-Constitution treaty/agreement disputes.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the advisory jurisdiction under Article 143?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 143, if it appears to the President that a question of law or fact has arisen or is likely to arise which is of such a nature and of such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the opinion of the Supreme Court, the President may refer the question to the Court for consideration. The Court may, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report to the President its opinion thereon. A special provision applies to certain disputes arising out of pre-Constitution treaties and agreements.

examTips: Advisory opinion on Presidential reference; public importance; not a contested decree.

keyTakeaways: Art 143: Presidential reference for advisory opinion of the SC.
